title: I Build Features Just By Talking to My Code
lesson: A process short can make an abstract interaction understandable by showing the trigger, the complete input, questions, approval and visible output. The input needs a sustained read window, and every later result must belong to that same input.
opening: The surprising spoken premise is talking to code. A /voice title and headphones on a product mascot cue listening, then a Space keycap identifies the trigger before the input window appears.
story_arc: Voice premise → spacebar action → long prompt accumulation → plan/activity montage → questions → research phase → approval condition and human approval illustration → model identity → build/test montage → website tour → completion cue → teammate metaphor → product CTA.
payoff: The short makes voice-to-request and the intended process stages recognisable. It does not close the opening dashboard request with a matching dashboard result: the shown output is a Mars registration website. Approval order, actual clarifying-question direction and successful verification are also not demonstrated cleanly.
selection_reason: Provides the strongest contrast to a two-second editing metronome: one input scene holds for more than six seconds after its brief entrance. It also distinguishes a whole-window enlargement, small keycap emphasis, accumulating questions, native UI scrolling and completion overlays from separate layout changes.
review_limits: All four complete chronological 2 fps context pages were inspected, plus three narrow 10 fps strips regenerated from explicit decoded source frame indices and a full-resolution output frame. No audio audition in this expansion. Spoken ideas are paraphrases of timed caption sidecars checked against the visible sequence. Beat boundaries remain approximate editorial partitions, generally within 0.5-second contextual spacing; exact frame-index strip labels support only the inspected intervals. No easing or word-perfect synchronisation is claimed. Machine captions extend beyond the visual duration; coverage ends at 30.1 seconds. These are source observations and proposed planning decisions, not a rendered replica or qualified template.

beats.camera_observation: The upper mascot gains headphones within the same split; the presenter remains below.
beats.camera_reason: The added headphones encode listening. The brand panel itself is orientation rather than demonstrated operation.
beats.pacing_reason: The short opening combines the surprising spoken premise with one simple visible cue.
beats.handoff: The next full presenter frame names the physical action used to start speaking.
beats.implementation_note: Reuse authorised product identity assets and a simple native title layer. If the voice function needs explanation, use a restrained listening cue or actual capture; do not build a mascot scene just for decoration.
beats.transfer: Use when the same concrete subject or action supports our spoken point.
beats.caution: This is an illustrative opening; the frames alone do not verify the product's voice behaviour.

beats.spoken_idea: The voice input begins with a request to build a customer-support dashboard.

beats.change: Cut from the preceding image to this framing.

beats.camera_reason: The enlargement introduces and makes the entire input more legible; it does not jump to a new field or result.
beats.pacing_reason: A short entrance establishes the input scene, followed by a much longer stable reading interval.
beats.handoff: The same window continues as the complete request accumulates.
beats.implementation_note: Capture the actual voice-to-input action if it is evidence. Native crop/scale is simplest; ui-focus-zoom is optional if a captured window needs a controlled whole-screen enlargement. Supply the real content and preserve its aspect ratio.
beats.transfer: Use an initial screen enlargement when the subsequent words would be too small, then hold the readable context.
beats.caution: The styled scene does not independently establish whether the typing came from live speech.

beats.spoken_idea: The requested dashboard should show tickets, filter by priority, assign teammates and look clean and modern.
beats.visible: The same listening window holds while the dashboard request grows line by line; the Space label remains below. No unrelated B-roll interrupts it.
beats.change: The introductory enlargement settles; the meaningful changes are accumulating requirements within the same input.
beats.why_this_picture: Keeping the whole request visible preserves the relationship among the requirements instead of turning each phrase into an unrelated graphic.
beats.camera_observation: Chronological context at 3.5–9.0 retains the input window; the early narrow strip shows the enlargement settling. The main continuing motion is text appearance, not repeated camera changes.
beats.camera_reason: The stable window lets the viewer follow one request from partial to complete. No new attention target requires a zoom.
beats.pacing_reason: This roughly six-second hold is purposeful: the prompt is the story's input and needs to accumulate and remain readable. It contradicts a mandatory two-second layout change.
beats.handoff: The complete request should hand off to a plan for this same dashboard; the next code example is only partial continuity.
beats.implementation_note: Reuse a native media capture or explicitly illustrative input scene. Preserve the full request across the hold; use a readable portrait crop before adding new chrome. Do not treat caption updates as new visual beats.
beats.transfer: Use when a multi-part input must be understood before its output can be evaluated.
beats.caution: Small prompt text still needs portrait QA. Reading can be supported by speech, but an actual input/result proof must retain the same project.
